decision: Limit this task to GitHub archive and catalog maintenance; keep producer roots read-only and exclude revoked or prohibited scopes and all external-record operations.
rationale: One owner and one writer prevents concurrent mutations and keeps custody evidence exact.

decision: Treat the classical, coverage-map, reader-root, and source-root source/receipt pairs as one linear published GitHub catalog chain.
rationale: A single chain makes exact custody and raw readback discoverable without replaying prior task transcripts.

decision: Index 12,407 source paths from Git tree and blob metadata instead of rereading 2,546,045,982 committed bytes.
rationale: Git identities bind paths, sizes, modes, and committed bytes while keeping disk and CPU load bounded; checkout-size differences remain separately visible.

decision: A root-level filesystem listing of manifests/published-github exceeded ten seconds and returned no filenames before timeout.
rationale: Broad receipt enumeration was unnecessary and risked avoidable machine load.

decision: Do not retry broad receipt-directory enumeration; derive maintenance history only from explicitly known task-owned commits and exact receipt paths.
rationale: The exact-commit route completed with bounded reads and preserves unrelated scope boundaries while retaining the failed attempt as history.

decision: The first append-helper replay converted an ISO timestamp string to a date object and rejected the valid first record before any second write.
rationale: Canonical hash verification must preserve JSON string types exactly.

decision: Parse existing JSONL timestamps as strings before canonical hash replay.
rationale: String-preserving parsing restores deterministic validation while leaving the first record byte-identical.

decision: Validate local navigation with an explicit 23-document GitHub-only scope; count external URLs without requesting them and stop before prohibited local targets.
rationale: A reusable bounded checker prevents stale catalog links without broad filesystem enumeration or external-record access.

decision: Route contribution, correction, source-suggestion, and pull-request intake through exact GitHub coverage maps, paths, commits, and byte hashes; treat external producer receipts as optional supporting evidence.
rationale: GitHub-first intake exposes existing unchecked or source-only translations before work begins and removes a required external-record dependency from issue reporting.

decision: A case-variant PR-template path in the audit and staging list left the repository canonical lowercase pull-request template outside the first local source commit.
rationale: The Windows checkout resolved both path spellings while Git staging and GitHub path identity remained case-sensitive.

decision: Use the canonical tracked lowercase PR-template path, regenerate the link manifest, and commit the omitted template before any remote push.
rationale: The corrective commit preserves the stopped local state while making the intended eleven-file GitHub-first intake checkpoint complete.

decision: A maintenance-log append attempt supplied a round-trip UTC offset ending in +00:00, which the helper contract rejected because it requires a trailing Z.
rationale: The exclusive helper stopped before mutation; the failed invocation must not be reinterpreted as an append.

decision: Format append timestamps as invariant UTC text with an explicit trailing Z before invoking the locked helper.
rationale: The corrected call satisfies the helper contract and preserves the rejected no-write attempt as a separate error record.

decision: The first commit-pinned readback compared two Git-normalized YAML blobs with CRLF checkout bytes and reported two false mismatches.
rationale: Git and the raw endpoint agreed byte-for-byte; only the comparison basis was wrong, so no remote content defect occurred.

decision: Bind link-audit and raw-readback identities to committed HEAD Git blobs and record checkout normalization separately.
rationale: The remote raw surface publishes committed blobs; using the same byte identity eliminates line-ending false positives without changing contributor content.

decision: The first batched Git target check timed out because it wrote all queries before draining the redirected output pipe.
rationale: Pipe backpressure blocked the bounded checker; the attempt produced no publication receipt and was not retried unchanged.

decision: Drain Git batch-check stdout and stderr asynchronously while writing the bounded target list.
rationale: Concurrent pipe drainage preserves the explicit 633-target scope and completes the 725-link audit without deadlock or filesystem enumeration.
